BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r1.claim: Al-Haqqa is a name for the Resurrection: from haqq, ‘to be due and established,’ since its coming is obligatory and certain; al-Raghib instead says recompense becomes due then, a figurative attribution. He cites 20:15.
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r1.anchor: هي منأسماء القيامة من حق يحق بالكسر إذا وجب وثبت لأنها يحق

BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r2.claim: ‘What is the Haqqa?’ originally asks what it is like in state and character; putting the explicit noun where a pronoun could stand underscores its majesty and terror.
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r2.anchor: الأصل ما هي أي أي شيء هي في حالها وصفتها فإن ما قد يطلب بها الصفة والحال فوضع الظاهر موضع المضمر

BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r3.claim: Exegetes parse the repeated question as nested nominal clauses, with the repeated noun linking them; the author’s preferred analysis makes interrogative ‘what’ the predicate, highlighting that the Haqqa is a wondrous, terrifying event.
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r3.anchor: ومقتضى التحقيق أن تكون ما الاستفهامية خبرا لما بعدها فإن مناط الفائدة بيان أن الحاقة أمر بديع وخطب فظيع

BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r4.claim: ‘What could make you know’ derives from knowledge and means ‘what informed you, Muhammad’; the question is parsed as a subject and predicate, with the following question as its second object.
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r4.anchor: من الدراة بمعنى العلم يقال دراه ودرى به أي علم به

BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r5.claim: The repeated question magnifies the Hour’s horror beyond the knowledge or imagination of creatures; whatever state one imagines is still less than it. One view says the Prophet knew it would occur but not its full manner; it may address hearers through him.
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r5.anchor: بحيث لا يكاد تبلغه دراية أحد ولا وهمه وكيفما قدرت حالها فهي أعظم من ذلك وأعظم

BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r6.claim: Inwardly, the Haqqa is the absolute singular manifestation within unity that annihilates all distinctions under the sovereignty of the One, the Subduer; it is called true because it is established in itself.
BURSEVI:v10p100#2/r6.anchor: يشير بالحاقة إلى التجلي الإحدى الإطلاقي في مراءة الواحدية المفني للكل

QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r3.claim: The question about the Inevitable Reality magnifies its importance and makes its gravity unmistakable.
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r3.anchor: استفهام يفيد التعظيم لأمرها ، والتفخيم لشأنها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r1.claim: The sentence may coordinate with “What is the Reality?” The second interrogative “what” conveys that people cannot comprehend the Reality's true nature because an extraordinary event is difficult to imagine.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r1.anchor: والاستفهام بها مكنى به عن تعذر إحاطة علم الناس بكنه الحاقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r2.claim: The addressee of “what made you know” is indefinite: the Reality is so great that its true nature is beyond your grasp.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r2.anchor: والمعنى : الحاقة أمر عظيم لا تدركون كنهه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r3.claim: “What made you know” is a fixed idiom built from interrogative mā and causative adrā, whose verb takes three objects; the first object's underlying role shifts under causation, while the second is suspended by the interrogative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r3.anchor: وتركيب ( ما أدراك كذا ) مما جرى مجرى المثل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r4.claim: The first mā magnifies by a rhetorical association between asking about extraordinary things and their greatness; it may instead be a question denying anyone knowledge, but both readings create awe.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r4.anchor: و { ما } الأولى استفهامية مستعملة في التهويل والتعظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r5.claim: The third mā suspends adrā from governing its two objects, and the masculine singular address is generic rather than directed to one person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r5.anchor: وكاف الخطاب فيه خطاب لغير معين فلذلك لا يقترن بضمير تثنية أو جمع أو تأنيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, and Yaḥyā ibn Sallām say every “what made you know” is later explained, unlike “what makes you know”; if sound, the former promises an outcome while the latter denies knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p113/r6.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس : كل شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib observes that Qur'anic “what made you know” formulas are followed by an explanation; Ibn ʿĀshūr takes this as clarifying the report from Ibn ʿAbbās and others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r1.anchor: وقال الراغب : كل موضع ذكر في القرآن { وما أدراك } فقد عقب ببيانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says grammarians have not adequately explained this construction, and some omit it altogether.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r2.anchor: ولم أر من اللغويين من وفى هذا التركيب حقه من البيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r4.claim: Alternatively, if the clauses connect, Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Resurrection; “the Striker” is a synonym for the Reality, brought forward instead of a pronoun to explain its terrifying force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r4.anchor: فعدل إلى إظهار اسم ( القارعة ) لأن ( القارعة ) مرادفة

NAHHAS:v5p19/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p19/r2.claim: ما الحاقة is parsed as subject and predicate and as a predicate about al-Haqqa; repeating the name adds grandeur and emphasis.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r2.anchor: مبتدأ وخبره وهما خبر عن الحاقة وفيه معنى التعظيم والتقدير الحاقة ما هي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r5.claim: 'What makes you know?' intensifies the point by invoking horrors and details beyond the listener's knowledge; the question also reproves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وما أدراك ما الحاقة مبالغة في هذا المعنى: أي أن فيها ما لم تدره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345#3/r1.claim: The Prophet had not witnessed the Inevitable and could not yet know the terrors it contains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345#3/r1.anchor: أي لأنك لم تعاينها ولم تدر ما فيها من الأهوال

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r1.claim: A report promises an easy reckoning from God for anyone who recites Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r1.anchor: من قرأ سورة (الحاقة) حاسبه الله حسابا يسيرا

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r2.claim: After the Resurrection warning in al-Qalam and the command to endure the unbelievers' abuse, al-Ḥāqqah opens with the Resurrection and its events.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر في سورة (القلم) حديث القيامة ووعيد الكفار،

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r6.claim: One explanation calls al-Ḥāqqah a name for the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r6.anchor: إنه اسم من أسماء القيامة، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r7.claim: Another derives it from “truth”: God's promise and threat become true at the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r7.anchor: لأن وعده ووعيده يحق فيها، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it is so called because the realities of deeds become clear there.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r8.anchor: لأنه يتبين فيها حقائق الأعمال فسميت الحاقة

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r9.claim: It can mean the inevitable event, when each person necessarily receives recompense for his deeds.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r9.anchor: الحاقة: الواجبة، من قولهم: حق، أي: وجب

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r10.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r10.claim: Al-Kisāʾī calls it the Day of truth; other explanations say it is a true event with no denial or a day that overpowers the unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r10.anchor: وقيل: سميت الحاقة؛ لأنها يوم الحق، عن الكسائي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r6.claim: Repeating the question about الحاقة magnifies and exalts its importance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r7.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r7.claim: He transmits the distinction that every Quranic “what made you know?” is followed by teaching, whereas “what could make you know?” concerns something not taught.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r7.anchor: سلام : بلغني أن كل شىء في القرآن فيه ( وما أدراك ) فقد أدراه إياه وعلمه إياه , وكل شيء قال فيه ( وما يدريك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r8.speaker: الأصم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r8.claim: He says the name الحاقة was unfamiliar in the Prophet's and his people's speech.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r8.anchor: وما أدراك ما هذا الاسم , لأنه لم يكن في كلامه ولا كلام قومه , قاله الأصم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r9.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r9.claim: Another reading of the question is, what will occur at the Resurrection?
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r9.anchor: وما أدراك ما يكون في الحاقة . { كذبت ثمود وعاد بالقارعة } أما ثمود فقوم صالح كانت منازلهم في الحجر فيما بين الشام والحجاز , قاله محمد بن

MUQATIL:69:1-4/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r2.claim: The question addressed to the Prophet magnifies the Hour because of its severity.
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r2.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: { ومآ أدراك ما الحاقة } [آية: 3] تعظيما لها لشدتها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p273#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p273#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p273#6/r1.claim: What could inform you of its nature? No creature can grasp the Hour's full greatness and severity; grammatically ما الحاقة begins a clause that serves as the second object of أدري.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p273#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ وما أدراك ﴾ وأي شيء أعلمك ﴿ ما الحاقة ﴾ يعني أنك لا علم لك بكنهها ومدى عظمها

QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r7.claim: The Prophet knew the Resurrection but not its full description, which he had not witnessed; the question magnifies it.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r7.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان عالما بالقيامة ولكن بالصفة.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r8.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r8.claim: Yahya ibn Salam says every Qur'anic “what made you know?” is followed by God teaching the matter.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r8.anchor: وقال يحيى بن سلام: بلغني أن كل شيء في القرآن «وما أدراك» فقد أدراه إياه وعلمه.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r9.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r9.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah distinguishes “what made you know?” as explained from “what will make you know?” as unexplained.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r9.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: كل شيء قال فيه: { ومآ أدراك } فإنه أخبر به

STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah is a late Makkan sūrah, generally dated shortly after al-Mulk, and named for the Day of Judgment in its opening verses.
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r1.anchor: A late Makkan sūrah, al-Ḥāqqah is generally believed to have been revealed shortly after Sūrah 67, al-Mulk.

STUDYQURAN:69:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r1.claim: Ḥāqqah is an emphatic form of ḥaqq, meaning truth or reality; here it evokes the overwhelming, inevitable reality none can avoid.
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r1.anchor: Undeniable Reality translates ḥāqqah, which is an emphatic form ofḥaqq, meaning “truth” or “reality.”

STUDYQURAN:69:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r5.claim: Repeating the question, as in 101:2–3, emphasizes that the Reality exceeds mere rational comprehension.
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r5.anchor: The repetition of the question in vv. 2–3, which is similar to that in 101:2–3

TAB-FULL:v23p207/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r1.claim: The question asks what could make Muhammad know or understand what the Inevitable is.
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وما أدراك ما الحاقة} [الحاقة: 3] تعظيما ليوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v23p207/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r2.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r2.claim: Sufyan observes a Quranic distinction: “what makes you know” is left unanswered, whereas “what has made you know” is followed by an explanation.
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r2.anchor: عن سفيان، قال: ما في القرآن: {وما يدريك} [الأحزاب: 63] فلم يخبره

TAB-FULL:v23p207/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r3.claim: Qatada says the question magnifies the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v23p207/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وما أدراك ما الحاقة} [الحاقة: 3] تعظيما ليوم القيامة كما تسمعون

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r4.claim: 'What could make you know what the Reality is?' asks what thing could inform the hearer about the Reality.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r4.anchor: معناه أي شيء أعلمك ما الحاقة

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r5.claim: The interrogative mā is nominative despite following adrāka, because a word in an interrogative construction is not governed by what precedes it.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r5.anchor: لأن ما كان في لفظ الاستفهام لا يعمل فيه ما قبله.

TABATABAI:69:1-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r5.claim: The author suggests Ibn Abbas's distinction may be intended: what made you know signifies God informed the Prophet, while what makes you know signifies something withheld.
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r5.anchor: ولعل هذا هو المراد مما نقل عن ابن عباس أن ما في القرآن من قوله تعالى

THALABI:v10p25#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p25#3/r5.claim: The first al-Ḥāqqah may be a subject whose predicate follows; alternatively it is explained by the second as an expression of wonder, like asking What is Zayd?
THALABI:v10p25#3/r5.anchor: والحاقة الأولى رفع بالابتداء وخبره فيما بعده، وقيل: الحاقة الأولى مرفوعة بالثانية

THALABI:v10p25#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p25#3/r6.claim: Thamud and Aad were struck by the calamity promised through their messengers; Ibn Abbas and Qatada alternatively identify the calamity as the Resurrection.
THALABI:v10p25#3/r6.anchor: كذبت ثمود وعاد بالقارعة أي بالعذاب الذي نزل بهم حين وعدهم نبيهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r1.claim: In mā al-ḥāqqah, the second al-ḥāqqah is the predicate and refers back to the first; the construction means, What is the Inevitable Reality?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r1.anchor: رفع بالابتداء أيضا، و {الحاقة} الثانية خبرها، والعائد على {الحاقة} الأولى الثانية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r2.claim: The question-form magnifies the event, as when one asks about someone to exalt or disparage him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r2.anchor: والمعنى تفخيم شأنها، واللفظ لفظ الاستفهام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r3.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the repeated question is to magnify and terrify, like the opening of al-Qāriʿah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: قوله: {ما الحاقة (2)} هو تفخيم وتهويل لها، (و) (¬4) مثله قوله: {القارعة (1) ما القارعة (2)}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r4.speaker: امرؤ القيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r4.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse is cited for an interrogative phrase that conveys magnification and awe.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r4.anchor:
امرؤ (¬5) القيس:
دع (¬6) عنك نهبا صيح في حجراته ... ولكن حديث ما حديث الرواحل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r5.claim: In wa-mā adrāka mā al-ḥāqqah, mā is nominative despite following adrāka because an interrogative term is not governed by what precedes; the sense is, What could make you know what it is?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r5.anchor: و {ما} موضعها رفع، وإن كان بعد "أدراك" لأن ما كان في لفظ الاستفهام لا يعمل فيه ما قبله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r6.claim: The language scholars say the address magnifies the Reality although the Prophet knows it, because he knows it by description; the expression treats it as though he did not know it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p131/r6.anchor: أهل المعاني: إنما قيل له: {وما أدراك ما الحاقة (3)} مع أنه يعلمها؛ لأنه إنما يعلمها بالصفة، فقيل تفخيما لشأنها

ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r1.claim: Asad renders al-haqqah as the laying-bare of truth, emphasizes its awe, and says its reality exceeds human conception.
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r1.anchor: OH, THE LAYING-BARE of the truth! [1] (69:2) How awesome that laying-bare of the truth! (69:3) And what could make thee conceive

ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n2/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n2/r1.claim: The ultimate reality will be beyond anticipation or imagination, which is why the rhetorical question receives no answer.
ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n2/r1.anchor: this sudden perception of the ultimate reality will be beyond anything that man can anticipate or imagine: hence, no answer is given

ELMALILI:69:2-5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r2.claim: Grammatically, the first ma is an interrogative subject, adra-ka is its predicate, the addressed pronoun is the first object, and the question what the Haqqa is forms the second object.
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r2.anchor: “Mâ” yine istifham için mübtedâ, “dirâyet”ten أَدْرَىٰكَ fiili haber

ELMALILI:69:2-5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r3.claim: No created being can comprehend the Haqqa's severity by estimation; its actual occurrence will disclose it, while beforehand it is known only through divine report and faith in that report cannot fully encompass its reality.
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r3.anchor: onun şiddet ve fezâ‘atinin azameti mahlûkāttan birinin dirayetiyle, tahmin ve takdîri ile bilinemez

ELMALILI:69:2-5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r4.claim: Those who disbelieve the transmitted report because reason cannot grasp the event dismiss it as superstition, fable, poetry, invention, or deception.
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r4.anchor: evhâm, masal, hurafe, şiir, uydurma, aldatma diye türlü laflarla tekzîbe kalkışırlar

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r3.claim: Treating mā al-Ḥāqqah as the predicate is an erroneous grammatical analysis.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r3.anchor: to be its khabar (enunciative) have made an erroneous conclusion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r4.claim: The truncated, ambiguous wording jolts an indifferent addressee by focusing attention on the opening subject and drawing attention through uncertainty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r4.anchor: The khabar is not mentioned so that all the attention of the addressee is focused on the mubtadā’.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r5.claim: Mā al-Ḥāqqah heightens dread: who can know what this inevitable event is and what will befall its stubborn deniers?
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r5.anchor: is a powerful expression of the horror and dreadfulness which is further explained by the subsequent words:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r6.claim: The same startling mode of address appears in al-Qāriʿah, where the author says he will explain it further.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r6.anchor: In Sūrah al-Qāri‘ah also, this style of address can be witnessed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and follows the previous surah's mention of the fortunate, the wretched, and deniers by describing Resurrection and its rewards and punishments, with past destroyed peoples as warnings to Meccans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية. ومناسبتها لما قبلها: أنه لما ذكر شيئا من أحوال السعداء والأشقياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r8.claim: What could make you know what the Resurrection is heightens the warning: its ordeals exceed what anyone could know or describe.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r8.anchor: وما أدراك ما الحاقة: مبالغة في التهويل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r1.claim: The root darā normally takes bi, sometimes omitted; with the causative hamza the two objects take different constructions, so mā al-ḥāqqah is accusative after the omitted preposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r1.anchor: وأصل درى أن يعدى بالباء، وقد تحذف على قلة، فإذا دخلت همزة النقل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r1.claim: The question stresses the Hour's terror and magnitude: it lies beyond creatures' knowledge or imagination, and every estimate of its horror falls short.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r1.anchor: تأكيد لهولها وفظاعتها ببيان خروجها عن دائرة علوم المخلوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r2.claim: The interrogative indirectly says that no awareness can reach or encompass it; the first “what” is a subject and “informed you” its predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r2.anchor: ومنه يعلم أن الإستفهام كني به عن لازمه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r3.claim: The clause “what is the Hour?” is in the accusative after an elided preposition, suspended as an indirect question, rather than serving as a second object governed directly by “informed.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r3.anchor: وما الحاقة جملة محلها النصب على إسقاط الخافض لا أن أدري يتعدى إلى المفعول الثاني بالباء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r4.claim: The question sentence as a whole coordinates with the preceding short clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#2/r4.anchor: والجملة أعني ما أدراك الخ معطوفة على ما قبلها من الجملة الصغرى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r5.claim: The Prophet could not know al-Haqqa because he had not seen it or witnessed its terrors.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r5.anchor: {وما أدراك ما الحاقة} أي أنك لا تعلمها إذ لم تعاينها ولم تر ما فيها من الأهوال.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:2-4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:2-4/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:2-4/r3.claim: No one can know the event's true nature, for it is beyond anyone's grasp; grammatically mā is subject and adrāka its predicate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:2-4/r3.anchor: أي أنك لا تعلم كنهها فإنها أعظم من أن تبلغها دراية أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r3.claim: ‘What has made you know’ refers to past knowledge and leaves the imagination open; no one can comprehend the Reality’s full nature before seeing it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r3.anchor: أي إنها بحيث لا يعلم كنهها أحد ولا يدركها ولا يبلغها درايته

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r7.claim: Al-Haqqa is the Hour, making each worker realize his deeds; the question magnifies the Resurrection, and al-Qariʿa also means the Hour.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {الحاقة} يعني الساعة أحقت لكل عامل عمله {وما أدراك ما الحاقة} قال: تعظيما ليوم القيامة

QASHANI:69:5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:5/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:5/r2.claim: The questions mean that no one but God knows the first Hour's horror and events, or the great Hour's reality, exalted rank, manifest proof, and disclosures.
QASHANI:69:5/r2.anchor: لا يعرف شدتها وهولها وما يظهر فيها من الأحوال على المعنى الأول

BURHAN:v2p337/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p337/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p337/r3.claim: Repeated questions can intimidate or magnify an event; ‘what do the criminals hasten?’ magnifies the punishment they seek to hasten.
BURHAN:v2p337/r3.anchor: ﴿ ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون ﴾ 3 تفخيم للعذاب الذي يستعجلونه
